subject: Partner trial top-up request: Forge Accelerator cohort - demo day extension
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <samantha@forge-accelerator.org>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short trial top-up for demo cohort (June 30)

Hi Lauren,

Hope you're well — Forge is running our demo day for the June cohort on June 30 and a handful of startups are in the final integration sprint. A few are right at the usage cap and we were wondering if Redwood could provide a one-time top-up of partner credits so these teams can finish demos and go-live tests without interruption.

Details:
- Cohort size: 12 startups (see attached list)
- Requested uplift: token-equivalent for roughly $3k USD total (estimate ~300k tokens)
- Time window requested: extend trial window to July 15 for the cohort participants

We can require individual startups to accept a short supplemental TOS if needed. If possible, we'd appreciate a quick approval by end of day Monday so the teams can proceed.

Thanks,
Samantha Reed
Community Programs Manager
Forge Accelerator
Samantha@forge-accelerator.org

Hi Samantha — thanks for the note and the cohort list.

Looping in Ben from Partnerships and Dev from Finance to confirm feasibility and the right mechanism (marketplace promo credits vs. one-off billing credit). Proposed quick plan:

- Redwood approves one-time promotional allocation equivalent to $3k total for the cohort.
- Forge confirms exact email list and start/end dates (requested: immediate -> 2027-07-15).
- We generate a small supplemental TOS and DocuSign packet for each startup (or a master agreement for Forge to accept).
- Ben/Dev to confirm whether credit will be applied via Marketplace code, Redwood account credit, or direct invoice adjustment.

Ben/Dev — are you OK with that approach? Also, any restrictions on distribution (per-company caps, single-use codes, etc.) we should send to the cohort?

Samantha — if you can confirm the final list and whether Forge prefers per-company codes or a single pool, we'll take it from there.

Best,

+1 to the approach. A couple of operational notes:

- Funding source: recommend we pull from the "Marketplace Accelerator Fund Q2" allocation. I attached a quick allocation breakdown.
- Distribution: per-company single-use promo codes are easiest for audit and expiry enforcement. We can generate 12 single-use codes capped at token-equivalents.
- Limits: suggest a per-company cap of $350 to keep individual spend predictable (12 x $350 = $4,200 ceiling; we can scale down to $250 if Finance prefers $3k).
- Compliance: need Dev to confirm there are no billing or tax complications for issuing partner promo codes to third parties.

If Finance signs off, Partnerships can generate codes and a one-page instruction doc for Forge to distribute to the cohort.

Ben
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Hey team — fine with a one-time promo allocation. A few controls I'd like in place before we issue codes:

1) Usage window strictly enforced: enable expiration 2027-07-15 23:59 UTC.
2) Per-company cap: $300 (12 x $300 = $3,600 total exposure). That keeps us within Q2 buffer.
3) Tracking: attach HubSpot deal ID and include the promo batch id so we can reconcile consumption.
4) Approvals: legal asked for a short supplementary TOS; I reviewed the draft and left two minor edits (attached).

Once Ben confirms the distribution mechanism (single-use codes), I authorize the allocation and will notify Finance to reserve the funds.
